label: Erbil Civilization Museum incantation bowl (2016 display)
summary: Pottery incantation bowl with Aramaic text displayed in the Erbil Civilization Museum; the caption's Seleucid attribution is anomalously early and retained only as a disputed reported claim.

source.title: Visiting the Erbil Civilization Museum
source.citation: Amin, Osama S. M. ‘Visiting the Erbil Civilization Museum.’ World History Foundation, 18 October 2016, object photograph and caption at lines 267–268.

claims.value_text: Erbil Civilization Museum, Erbil, Iraqi Kurdistan
Modern-day Iraq; precise excavation provenance unknown

claims.notes: The caption's dating is much earlier than the usual late-antique incantation-bowl corpus and requires expert review.

media.notes: Photograph by Osama S. M. Amin.

label: Kedem Auction 32 lot 153
summary: Jewish Babylonian Aramaic incantation bowl offered by Kedem in 2013 to protect the house, threshold, and shop of Ḥušaʾa son of Šīlta.

source.title: Incantation Bowl — Auction 32 lot 153
source.citation: Kedem Auction House. ‘Incantation Bowl.’ Auction 32, lot 153, 2 July 2013.

claims.value_text: Protection and prosperity for the client's house, threshold, and shop

texts.content: The text identifies itself as an amulet for the house, dwelling, threshold, and shop of Ḥušaʾa son of Šīlta, asking that grace and mercy be released upon his buying and selling as rain is released from heaven.

label: Christie's 2000 lot 734 / Artemis Gallery item 146419
summary: Large Judeo-Aramaic love-restoration bowl for Bar-Imma son of Sukhtoy and Parkoy daughter of Abanduk, sold at Christie's in 2000 and reoffered in 2019.

source.title: 7th C. Mesopotamian Incantation Bowl, ex-Christie's
source.citation: Artemis Gallery. ‘7th C. Mesopotamian Incantation Bowl, ex-Christie's,’ lot 113, item 146419, Bidsquare product 1500258, 26 September 2019; ex Christie's New York, 7 December 2000, lot 734.

claims.value_text: Bar-Imma son of Sukhtoy; Parkoy daughter of Abanduk
Restoration of love and release from demons appearing in dreams
Central figure, perhaps Lilith, with snakes and a scorpion

events.details: Sold as Antiquities lot 734 for US$28,200.
Auction-reported provenance after the Christie's sale.

source.citation: Ostracon Ancient Art. ‘Mesopotamian Incantation Bowl, 5th–7th Century AD,’ Trocadero item 1495910, accessed 4 September 2026.

Bound male and female figures with a segmented scorpion
